headline: High: aci’s broad networked CRM/email integrations can leak or cascade data into Great Expectations workflows, while shared file/workspace assumptions remain unproven.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can ingest and emit content through APIs, email, Slack, Notion, and MCP, so malicious text could reach Great Expectations only if an operator bridges outputs into files or docs. Great Expectations primarily reads files and validation artifacts, so the interaction is possible but not default. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this low rather than none.
conditions: IF aci outputs are copied into files that Great Expectations parses as test definitions or docs
IF a shared MCP or workspace bridge is configured between aci and Great Expectations
mitigations: Keep aci outputs out of GE config directories
Use a read-only handoff folder
Require human review before importing text into GE
Disable any shared clipboard or MCP bridge
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on imported artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, while Great Expectations reads and writes files such as validation results and documentation. If they share a workspace, sensitive records can be copied into GE artifacts or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default operator workflows, but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF aci exports CRM/email/calendar data into a shared directory
IF Great Expectations stores validation results or docs in the same workspace containing sensitive inputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces by agent
Restrict GE inputs to synthetic samples
Review validation outputs for embedded secrets
Rotate any exposed OAuth or API secrets
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci supports multiple instances and can call external services; Great Expectations can install packages and manipulate files, but its network egress is none. The profiles do not show both agents writing the same mutable resource by default, so direct conflict is limited. If they are pointed at the same files or shared integrations, contention becomes more plausible, but that is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same workspace files
IF aci writes integration outputs while Great Expectations rewrites validation artifacts in the same directory
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run GE on copies of source data
Avoid concurrent package changes during validation
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM or research outputs that Great Expectations may later validate or document, creating a handoff where B could treat A’s content as authoritative. Great Expectations is not shown to independently verify semantic claims, only data quality artifacts, so bad upstream outputs can cascade into downstream reports. The pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes files produced by aci without an independent review step
IF aci-generated records are used as the source of truth for validation or reporting
mitigations: Insert a human review gate
Validate against an independent source
Mark aci outputs as untrusted inputs
Compare samples before publishing reports
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Aci handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data with broad network egress, while Great Expectations processes data sources and validation results in files. If EU personal data or regulated records are moved from aci into GE artifacts, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is exported from aci into Great Expectations files
IF the two agents are used under different retention or residency policies
mitigations: Classify data before transfer
Exclude regulated fields from validation sets
Set short retention on GE outputs
Document the data flow in a register
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
